title: Jamaica Raises Rates to 6.5% as Inflation Hits 8.2% | Across the Water, Ep. 18
lede: On Nov 18, 2026, the Bank of Jamaica raised its policy rate by half a point to 6.50%, effective Nov 19, its second rise since September. Inflation was 8.2% in October, the fifth straight month above the 4–6% target, driven by transport, food and utilities, commodity prices, El Niño and post-Hurricane Melissa rebuilding. This episode explains the decision, what it means for borrowers and growth, and why the money Jamaicans abroad send home now buys less.
keyPoints: The Bank of Jamaica raised its policy rate 50 basis points to 6.50%, effective Nov 19, 2026, by unanimous vote; it was 6.00% from Sep 29 and 5.75% a year earlier (BOJ; Jamaica Gleaner).
Annual inflation was 8.2% in October 2026, up from 2.9% a year earlier; transport rose 15.0% and food 10.9% (STATIN via BOJ and Jamaica Gleaner).
The BOJ expects inflation to peak in the March 2027 quarter and return to its 4–6% target by late 2027; it projects 0.5–1.5% real growth for FY2026/27 (BOJ).
Remittances were 15.4% of GDP in 2025 and US$1.78 billion in January–June 2026, up 4.2%, with 68.8% from the US in June (BOJ Remittance Bulletin).
The next BOJ policy decision is due Dec 18, 2026 (Jamaica Gleaner).
